request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an **Export** button (`data-testid="person-export"`) that downloads that row as `person-<id>.csv`. The file has a `cell,value` header, then one line for each of the 10 cells in the requested order. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **Where:** the change is entirely in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/features/people/PeopleList.tsx`. It works out each value with the same expression the row uses to display it, and builds the file with the app's existing `downloadCsv` helper. A value containing a comma is wrapped in quotes, e.g. `"Lee, Jo (B)"`. No server or stored-data changes were needed.
- **Hidden columns:** the export still includes cells whose column is switched off in the column chooser (claimed, due-total, aliases, hold and so on). It uses the value the row would show if the column were visible. The tests don't cover hidden columns. If you'd rather leave hidden cells out or blank, that's a small change.

I also added a two-line comment describing the button to the existing comment block at the top of that file, next to the other export buttons.
